Hi there—my name is Claire, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days, and it helps us spot anything from normal new-mom ups-and-downs to signs of depression or anxiety that might need extra support. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell us someone is in danger. There are no right or wrong answers—just whatever is true for you today. Ready to start?

1. Over the last seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?
Most of the time I can still laugh—maybe not quite as easily as before I had the baby, but usually once a day something will make me chuckle.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, like I said, most of the time I can still laugh—maybe not quite as easily as before I had the baby, but usually once a day something will make me chuckle.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
Sometimes… I still look forward to little things—like my morning coffee or when my mom comes over—but it’s not the same excitement I used to feel. It’s kind of dulled, I guess.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Like when the baby wouldn’t settle and I kept thinking maybe I’m just not doing something right, or when I dropped a bottle and spilled pumped milk—I felt pretty lousy about that, even though rationally I know accidents happen.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I do get little spurts of worry—like I’ll suddenly think, “Is she breathing?” even when she’s right next to me in the bassinet. It passes pretty quickly once I check on her, but yeah, it pops up a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky, more like a quick flutter of “what if something’s wrong?”—but it’s gone as fast as it comes. No full-on scares or anything.
Things have been getting on top of me
Some days, yeah. Like yesterday—she wouldn’t nap unless I held her, laundry was piling up, and I felt as if I was barely treading water. I managed, but it felt stressful for a bit.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, my mood hasn’t really messed with sleep. I drift off pretty easily once she’s down—only trouble is if she wakes a lot, then it’s hard to fall back asleep, but it’s not because I’m unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve had a couple of teary moments—like yesterday when I couldn’t get her to latch and I just felt this wave of sadness—but it’s not an all-day thing. It comes and goes.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried maybe twice this week. Once was after that rough feeding session, and once when my partner found me folding laundry at midnight and asked if I was okay—something about being seen just made the tears spill over.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I want to be here for my baby, and I’d never do anything like that.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, <2 wks after delivery  

1. Positive findings (frequency/intensity)  
- Anhedonia: diminished enjoyment (“dulled” excitement)  
- Labile mood: 2 crying spells this week, brief waves of sadness  
- Excessive guilt: self-blame over routine infant-care events  
- Anxiety: 3–4× daily intrusive “is she breathing?” worries; no full panic attacks  
- Overwhelm: reports “treading water” on difficult days  

2. Negative / low-level findings  
- Laughing retained (daily)  
- No sleep-onset problems (wake-ups infant-related)  
- No self-harm ideation  

3. Risk factors relevant to perinatal mood disorders  
- Mild anhedonia + tearfulness  
- Heightened, though brief, anxiety  
- Self-criticism/guilt  
- Acute situational stress (infant care, household tasks)  

4. Safety  
- Denies any thoughts of harming self; no suicidal ideation voiced.  

5. Screening impression  
Meets some criteria suggesting possible perinatal depression/anxiety; symptoms sub-clinical to mild, no impairment in basic functioning, no safety concerns at present. Continue monitoring; consider formal EPDS and follow-up within 1–2 wks or sooner if symptoms worsen or safety changes.
